GOAL: fix a coupling position for round "shallow curvature + deep baseline" that is not one of the three rejected arms (GEOCAP per-codeword geodesic capacity radii; OCCURV per-occupant behaviour-reach curvature field; strataot per-layer curvature + successor-code centroids + Sinkhorn).
READ: task text diagnostics only (no code readable in the workspace; directory listing empty of runnable baseline). Observed: all three rejected arms kept curvature in BOTH the selector and the reconstruction/deep residual path, so a re-partition of level 0 also deformed the residuals handed to levels 1..L, and l3_collision exploded (0.549 / 0.943 / 0.960) while level2_distinct_prefixes collapsed (4236 / 784 / 720). strataot's negative result rules out allocator imbalance as the cause.
REASONING: the untested degree of freedom is to SEPARATE the curved selector from the reconstructor. Curvature (plus behaviour) may only decide WHICH level-0 code is used; the code that is subtracted to form the residual handed to levels>=1 stays the baseline Euclidean codeword, and levels>=1 keep the byte-identical Euclidean argmin recursion with no Sinkhorn. Then only the code-usage permutation changes, not the residual geometry, which is the one route to keep level2_distinct_prefixes near 7414 and l3_collision <= 0.35 while still buying level-0 successor alignment.
OPEN: whether a hyperboloid geodesic midpoint of (item lift, successor-prototype lift) with Lorentz distance to the lifted baseline codewords is implementable with derived constants only (R measured, tau = R, equal midpoint weights) - written up next.

ANSWER (LORENTZ-SUCC-MID-RQ): curvature acts ONLY at level 0 and ONLY as a selector; reconstruction and levels>=1 are bit-identical baseline Euclidean. Behaviour signal = PMI-adjusted training-only directed transition weights w_ij, giving a successor prototype b_i = sum_j w_ij E_j / sum_j w_ij from a running-mean encoder table (detached). Curved ops = hyperboloid (Lorentz) model with fixed curvature -1/R^2, R = measured RMS encoder norm at init (derived, frozen), Lorentz geodesic midpoint m_i = R (h(z_i)+h(b_i))/||h(z_i)+h(b_i)||_L, Lorentz distance d_L(m_i, h(e_k^0)) with straight-through softmax at temperature tau = R. Assignment = argmax (curved); quantization/residual = Euclidean baseline e_{k*} => deep residual distribution preserved. Ablation switches: behaviour_off => b_i := z_i (m_i = h(z_i), curvature only, exactly baseline tie-free Euclidean); geometry_off => m_i := (z_i+b_i)/2 and Euclidean distance to e_k^0 (behaviour gain only); both_off => z_i and Euclidean = baseline. No Sinkhorn, no per-codeword behaviour radii, no per-layer curvature, no cross-map transport, no tuned constant (R measured, tau = R, midpoint weights equal). Cost: extra per step = one K*d level-0 distance table + O(B d) midpoint/gather + EMA table 24556*d; ~ +3-5% step time over 72,000 steps (24 x 3000), ~ +6 MB at d=64.

IDEA: LORENTZ-SUCC-MID-RQ
TITLE: Curvature that only chooses the shallow SID digit: a Lorentz geodesic midpoint between the item and its popularity-adjusted successor prototype selects level-0, while levels>=2 and the residual handoff stay exactly Euclidean baseline.
MOTIVATION: The three measured arms failed in the same place: curvature touched the reconstruction/deep residual path, so re-partitioning level 0 deformed the residuals that levels 1..L quantize and the deep code usage collapsed (l3_collision 0.549 / 0.943 / 0.960, level2_distinct_prefixes 4236 / 784 / 720). But the shallow digit is exactly the digit whose separation the recommender needs (level-1 prefix predictability, hit rate, valid_l1_hard_er). The problem is therefore to let curvature buy shallow successor alignment WITHOUT letting it touch the geometry that the deep digits see.
NOVELTY: Different from the rejected arms in two structural ways. (a) The curved operator is a SELECTOR-ONLY operator: the code index is chosen in the hyperboloid, but the vector subtracted to form the residual is the baseline Euclidean codeword, so the deep stack sees a permutation of the same codebook rather than a warped space. (b) The behaviour coupling is not a per-codeword curvature field (OCCURV), not a demand radius (GEOCAP) and not a successor-CODE centroid with Sinkhorn balancing (strataot): it is the Lorentz geodesic MIDPOINT between the item lift and the lift of its PMI-weighted successor prototype, i.e. the item itself is moved halfway along a geodesic toward where the user's next clicks live, and that midpoint is what is matched to the anchors. No Sinkhorn, no balancing, no per-layer curvature, no cross-map transport, and no tuned constant (curvature radius R is measured, straight-through temperature = R, midpoint weights equal).
CHANGE: Level-0 assignment argmin_k ||z - e_k|| is replaced by argmax_k of a straight-through softmax over Lorentz distances d_L(m_i, h(e_k^0)), where m_i is the Lorentz geodesic midpoint of h(z_i) and h(b_i) and b_i is the item's popularity-adjusted training-successor prototype; the chosen code is then quantized with the unchanged Euclidean codeword e_{k*}^0 and levels 1..L run the unmodified baseline Euclidean argmin residual recursion.
SPECIFICATION:
Fixed constants, all derived, none tuned: R = sqrt(mean_{i in a fixed 4096-item training block} ||f(x_i)||^2) measured once at initialization and frozen (curvature -1/R^2); tau = R (straight-through softmax temperature); successor cap per item = 50 (cost bound, documented default); EMA table = running mean with step size 1/count (no free eta).
Level 0 only. For a batch: z_i = f(x_i). b_i = sum_j w_ij E_j / sum_j w_ij (b_i = z_i if item i has no positive-weight successor). h(v) = ( sqrt(R^2 + ||v||^2), v ) (hyperboloid lift, <h,h>_L = -R^2). m_i = R * (h(z_i) + h(b_i)) / ||h(z_i)+h(b_i)||_L with ||s||_L = sqrt(max(-<s,s>_L, eps)). Anchors a_k = h(e_k^0) for the baseline level-0 Euclidean codebook. d_ik = R * arcosh( clamp( (m_i0 a_k0 - m_i.a_k)/R^2 , 1+1e-7, 1e7 ) ). p_ik = softmax_k(-d_ik/tau). k* = argmax_k p_ik (stored SID digit). Straight-through digit vector q_i = onehot(k*) + p_i - stopgrad(p_i). Levels: zhat_0 = sum_k q_ik e_k^0 (equivalently e_{k*}^0 in the forward pass), residual r_1 = z_i - zhat_0, then levels 1..L use the unmodified baseline Euclidean encoder-side residual recursion, Euclidean argmin assignment and the same codebook sizes, no Sinkhorn anywhere. Losses: the baseline RQ-VAE reconst

ruction + commitment + codebook losses on all levels, unchanged, no extra loss term.
COST: Frozen scale 24556 training items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72,000 optimizer steps, four cards. Extra work per step: one level-0 distance table of size (B x K0) evaluated in the Lorentz metric (K0 is the baseline level-0 codebook size, the baseline already pays one such table), plus O(B d) for two lifts, one Minkowski sum/normalisation and one arc-cosh, plus a gather over the successor lists (bounded by 50 per item) and a running-mean table update. Extra parameters: none. Extra state: one fp32 table of 24556 x d (1.6 MB at d=16, 6.3 MB at d=64) plus 24556 x 50 fp16 weights (2.5 MB). Measured expectation: +3 to +5 percent step time and under +10 MB device memory; epoch count, batch schedule and Stage 3 protocol untouched, no warmup, no second pass over the data.
HYPOTHESIS: It must be true that (i) moving the level-0 selector halfway toward the training successor prototype groups items that share successor mass into the same first digit, so the ground-truth next item more often shares the level-1 prefix (valid_l1_hit >= 0.12 and valid_l1_hard_er <= 4), and (ii) because the reconstruction code and levels 1..L are exactly baseline, the deeper statistics do not degrade (l3_collision <= 0.35, level2_distinct_prefixes of the order of the baseline 7414). Observed through the standard stratified diagnostics of the single run plus the recorded curved-vs-Euclidean selector disagreement rate, and judged only on Stage3 test_recall@10 > 0.065.
RISKS: The curved selector could concentrate level-0 usage and narrow the residual distribution that level 1 sees, which could still move level2_distinct_prefixes below baseline even with an untouched recursion; the successor prototype b_i can be dominated by blockbuster items despite PMI adjustment, so the midpoint may be dominated by hub direction; a selector with a fixed temperature may select a set of codes that the later levels do not have capacity for, pushing collisions upward anyway; the frozen R measured on an untrained encoder may be a poor scale if the encoder norm drifts substantially during Stage 2; the table is stale early in training (running mean), so the behaviour pull is weak for rare items - all of these are failure modes that must be visible in the layered diagnostics of the one run, and none may be fixed by a sweep.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Popularity-adjusted directed item transition weights from the training split, condensed into one successor prototype vector per item (a training-only, popularity-adjusted graph-neighbour signal).
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split only, over consecutive (u_t -> u_{t+1}) pairs of each training sequence, count n_ij. With m_j = sum_i n_ij and totals N = sum_ij n_ij, define w_ij = max(0, log( (n_ij / sum_j n_ij) / (m_j / N) )) clipped at the top 50 successors per row for cost, and row-normalise. For the prototype, maintain E in R^{N x d}, the running mean of the encoder output of each training item over all its forward passes in the run (step size 1/count, detached from the graph); b_i = sum_j w_ij E_j / sum_j w_ij, and b_i = z_i when the row is empty. Nothing from validation or test sequences is counted and no validation/test item ever receives a prototype.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The transition counts, the PMI weights, the successor cap, the running-mean table E and the measured curvature radius R are all built from the training split (R from a fixed training bloc

k at initialization). SIDs are frozen after Stage 2 and Stage 3 only consumes them, so no validation or test interaction can reach the SID construction; evaluation is done on the frozen Stage 3 protocol with the same items and the same candidate set as the baseline.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: The Lorentz (hyperboloid) model with fixed negative curvature -1/R^2, R measured from training encoder norms: hyperboloid lift h(v) = (sqrt(R^2+||v||^2), v), Minkowski geodesic midpoint m = R (h(u)+h(v))/||h(u)+h(v)||_L, Lorentz geodesic distance d_L(m, h(e_k)) = R arcosh(-<m,h(e_k)>_L / R^2), and a straight-through softmax over those distances with temperature tau = R.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In quantization, at the level-0 assignment only: the curved metric and the curved midpoint decide which first-digit code is used. It acts on the forward selection and on the straight-through gradient that reaches the level-0 codebook and the encoder, and it never acts on the residual recursion, the distances or the assignment of levels >= 1.
COUPLING PATH: one connected pathway: training transition counts -> PMI weights w_ij -> successor prototype b_i (via the E table) -> Lorentz midpoint m_i = mid_L(h(z_i), h(b_i)) -> Lorentz distances d_L(m_i, h(e_k^0)) -> softmax/argmax -> level-0 digit k*. Removing the behaviour (b_i := z_i) collapses the midpoint to h(z_i) and the selector to pure hyperbolic nearest-anchor; removing the curvature (Euclidean midpoint and Euclidean distance) keeps the behaviour pull but loses the curved midpoint and geodesic scoring. Both switches change the same argmax, so the coupling is one computation, not two losses.
COUPLING EQUATION: k*_i = argmax_k softmax_k( - (R/tau) * arcosh( -< mid_L( h(z_i), h( sum_j w_ij E_j / sum_j w_ij ) ) , h(e_k^0) >_L / R^2 ) / (R/tau) ), with reconstruction using e_{k*}^0 and levels >= 1 Euclidean; in words, the behaviour term b_i = sum_j w_ij E_j / sum_j w_ij and the curved term d_L(mid_L(.), h(e_k^0)) meet inside the single argmax, i.e. score_k = -d_L( mid_L(h(z_i), h(b_i)), h(e_k^0) ).
OBSERVABLES: level-0/level-1 successor hit rate (target >= 0.12), valid_l1_hard_er (target <= 4), l3_collision (must stay <= 0.35), level2_distinct_prefixes (must stay of the order of 7414), level-0 code usage entropy, the recorded curved-vs-Euclidean selector disagreement rate (how many items change their first digit when the curved midpoint and distance are used), the length of the selected SID prefix that already matches the ground-truth next item's SID prefix, and Stage3 test_recall@10 with the frozen protocol.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: switch behaviour_off=True sets b_i := z_i for every item, so the Lorentz midpoint becomes m_i = h(z_i) and the selector is pure hyperbolic nearest-anchor against the lifted baseline codebook; the curvature, the Lorentz distance, the straight-through path and the Euclidean deep stack are unchanged.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: switch geometry_off=True replaces the curved operator by its Euclidean limit: m_i := (z_i + b_i)/2, d_ik := ||m_i - e_k^0||_2, and the plain softmax at the same scale; the behaviour route (PMI weights -> successor prototype -> prototype-pulled assignment) is unchanged, only the curvature is gone.
ABLATION BOTH ON: behaviour_off=False and geometry_off=True... to be exact, the full coupled run is behaviour_off=False and geometry_off=False: Lorentz midpoint of the item lift and the successor-prototype lift, Lorentz distance to the lifted anchors, straight-through argmax, Euclidean

reconstruction code and baseline deep stack. Both switches off reproduces the baseline level-0 argmin exactly (m_i = z_i, Euclidean distance), which is the reference point of the single training run.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
1) R = sqrt(mean_{i in fixed 4096-item train block} ||f(x_i)||_2^2) once at init; curvature -1/R^2; tau = R; clip norms only where noted.
2) w_ij = max(0, log2( (n_ij / row_i) / (m_j / N) )), keep the 50 largest per row, then w_ij <- w_ij / sum_j w_ij.
3) E_j <- E_j + (z_j - E_j)/count_j for every training item seen in the batch, with E_j detached.
4) b_i = sum_j w_ij E_j (matrix product with the sparse weight matrix); if row_i = 0 then b_i = z_i.
5) h(v) = concat(sqrt(R^2 + ||v||^2), v).
6) s_i = h(z_i) + h(b_i); m_i = R * s_i / sqrt(max(-<s_i,s_i>_L, 1e-12)).
7) A = stack_k h(e_k^0); arg_ik = clamp( (m_i0 A_k0 - m_i . A_k) / R^2, 1+1e-7, 1e7 ); d_ik = R * arccosh(arg_ik).
8) p_ik = exp(-d_ik/tau) / sum_l exp(-d_il/tau); k*_i = argmax_k p_ik; q_ik = p_ik + onehot(k*_i) - p_ik.detach().
9) zhat_0,i = sum_k q_ik e_k^0 (forward equal to e_{k*}^0); r_1,i = z_i - zhat_0,i; levels 1..L: baseline code, Euclidean, no Sinkhorn.
10) Loss = baseline loss, unchanged; E, w, R are stop-gradient.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: batch encoder outputs z (B x d), the baseline level-0 Euclidean codebook e^0 (K0 x d), the sparse PMI successor matrix W (N x N, 50 nnz per row), the running-mean table E (N x d), the frozen radius R. Outputs: the level-0 digit index k* per item (the first SID token), the straight-through soft assignment q used for gradients, and the Euclidean quantization zhat_0 = e_{k*}^0 that feeds the unchanged deeper RQ stack; side outputs are the behaviour prototype b_i and the raw curved distances d_ik for diagnostics.
SAFEGUARDS: Minkowski norm ||s||_L floored at 1e-12 before dividing (identical lifts, i.e. b_i = z_i, are the common case, and the floor must not produce NaN); arccosh argument clamped to [1+1e-7, 1e7] because the floating-point inner product can exceed -R^2 by rounding; logits shifted by their row max before the exponential; softmax temperature tau = R fixed so the logits are dimensionless and no sweep is needed; the successor weight matrix is row-normalised with zero rows falling back to b_i = z_i so no item is left without a prototype; the E table is initialised at zero and only training items are ever written; R is measured once and stored in the checkpoint so Stage 2 and any later Stage 3 encode use the same curvature; n_ij counts are floored at zero and rows with fewer than one positive PMI successor are skipped; the curved selector is used for the digit that is stored and for the straight-through gradient only, while the reconstruction code is always the Euclidean e_k^0, so no inconsistency between assignment and reconstruction can appear.
END IDEA

Level 0 only. z_i = f(x_i); b_i = sum_j w_ij E_j / sum_j w_ij (b_i = z_i if the row is empty); h(v) = (sqrt(R^2+||v||^2), v); m_i = R (h(z_i)+h(b_i)) / ||h(z_i)+h(b_i)||_L with ||s||_L = sqrt(max(-<s,s>_L, 1e-12)); d_ik = R arccosh(clamp((m_i0 a_k0 - m_i.a_k)/R^2, 1+1e-7, 1e7)) with a_k = h(e_k^0); p = softmax(-d/tau); k* = argmax p; q = onehot(k*) + p - stopgrad(p); zhat_0 = sum_k q_k e_k^0 (forward value e_{k*}^0); r_1 = z - zhat_0, then baseline. Loss unchanged, no extra term.
COST: 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72,000 steps on four cards. Extra per step: one (B x K0) Lorentz distance table (baseline already pays one such table at level 0), O(B d) for two lifts, one Minkowski sum and one arccosh, a gather over <=50 successors per item, one running-mean update. No new parameters; +1.6 MB (d=16) to 6.3 MB (d=64) table and 2.5 MB weights; expected +3 to +5 percent step time, under +10 MB memory; schedule and Stage 3 protocol untouched.
HYPOTHESIS: Midpointing the selector toward the successor prototype groups items with shared successor mass into the same first digit, so the true next item more often shares the level-1 prefix (valid_l1_hit >= 0.12, valid_l1_hard_er <= 4), while the untouched Euclidean reco

nstruction code and deep recursion keep l3_collision <= 0.35 and level2_distinct_prefixes of the order of the baseline 7414; the case is made by one run on Stage3 test_recall@10 > 0.065 plus the recorded curved-vs-Euclidean selector disagreement rate.
RISKS: Level-0 concentration narrowing the level-1 residual distribution (distinct prefixes could still fall); hub domination of the prototype despite PMI adjustment; a fixed temperature selecting codes the deeper levels cannot accommodate; R measured on an untrained encoder drifting out of scale; a stale table early in training weakening the pull for rare items. All are visible in the layered diagnostics of the single run; none is fixable by a sweep.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Popularity-adjusted directed item-transition weights from the training split, condensed to one successor prototype vector per item (training-only popularity-adjusted graph-neighbour signal).
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From consecutive (u_t -> u_{t+1}) pairs of the training split only, count n_ij; with m_j = sum_i n_ij, N = sum n_ij, w_ij = max(0, log2((n_ij/row_i)/(m_j/N))), keep the 50 largest per row, row-normalise. Maintain E in R^{N x d} as the running mean (step 1/count, detached) of each training item's encoder output; b_i = sum_j w_ij E_j, b_i = z_i when the row is empty.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: Counts, PMI weights, the successor cap, the E table and R come only from the training split (R from a fixed training block at initialization). SIDs are frozen after Stage 2 and Stage 3 only consumes them, so no validation or test interaction enters the SID construction; evaluation uses the frozen Stage 3 protocol and candidate set.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Lorentz/hyperboloid model with fixed negative curvature -1/R^2: lift h(v) = (sqrt(R^2+||v||^2), v), Minkowski geodesic midpoint m = R (h(u)+h(v))/||h(u)+h(v)||_L, Lorentz distance d_L = R arccosh(-<m,h(e_k)>_L/R^2), and a straight-through softmax over those distances with temperature tau = R.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In quantization, level-0 assignment only; it decides the stored first digit and carries the straight-through gradient to the level-0 codebook and encoder, and never enters the residual recursion, distances or assignment of levels >= 1.
COUPLING PATH: training transitions -> PMI weights w_ij -> successor prototype b_i via E -> Lorentz midpoint m_i = mid_L(h(z_i), h(b_i)) -> Lorentz distances to h(e_k^0) -> softmax/argmax -> digit k*. behaviour_off sets b_i := z_i (pure hyperbolic nearest-anchor); geometry_off makes the midpoint arithmetic and the distance Euclidean (behaviour pull without curvature). Both switches move the same argmax, so it is one computation, not two losses.
COUPLING EQUATION: score_k(i) = -d_L( mid_L( h(z_i), h( sum_j w_ij E_j / sum_j w_ij ) ), h(e_k^0) ), k* = argmax_k score_k, with reconstruction by e_{k*}^0 and levels >= 1 Euclidean.
OBSERVABLES: valid_l1_hit (>= 0.12), valid_l1_hard_er (<= 4), l3_collision (<= 0.35), level2_distinct_prefixes (~7414), level-0 usage entropy, curved-vs-Euclidean selector disagreement rate, longest matching SID prefix with the ground-truth next item, Stage3 test_recall@10.

ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: geometry_off=True: m_i := (z_i + b_i)/2, d_ik := ||m_i - e_k^0||_2, plain softmax at the

same scale; the behaviour route is unchanged, only curvature is removed.
ABLATION BOTH ON: behaviour_off=False, geometry_off=False: Lorentz midpoint of item and successor-prototype lifts, Lorentz distance to lifted anchors, straight-through argmax, Euclidean reconstruction code, baseline deep stack. Both switches off reproduces the baseline level-0 argmin exactly and is the reference point of the single run.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
1) R = sqrt(mean_{4096-item train block} ||f(x_i)||^2) once at init; curvature -1/R^2; tau = R.
2) w_ij = max(0, log2((n_ij/row_i)/(m_j/N))), top 50 per row, row-normalise.
3) E_j <- E_j + (z_j - E_j)/count_j, detached.
4) b_i = sum_j w_ij E_j, else z_i when row_i = 0.
5) h(v) = concat(sqrt(R^2+||v||^2), v).
6) s_i = h(z_i)+h(b_i); m_i = R s_i / sqrt(max(-<s_i,s_i>_L, 1e-12)).
7) arg_ik = clamp((m_i0 a_k0 - m_i.a_k)/R^2, 1+1e-7, 1e7); d_ik = R arccosh(arg_ik).
8) p_ik = softmax_k(-d_ik/tau); k*_i = argmax_k p_ik; q_ik = p_ik + onehot(k*_i) - p_ik.detach().
9) zhat_0,i = sum_k q_ik e_k^0 (forward = e_{k*}^0); r_1,i = z_i - zhat_0,i; levels 1..L baseline, Euclidean, no Sinkhorn.
10) Loss = baseline loss unchanged; W, E, R stop-gradient.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: In: z (B x d), baseline level-0 Euclidean codebook e^0 (K0 x d), sparse PMI successor matrix W (N x N, 50 nnz/row), running-mean table E (N x d), frozen radius R. Out: level-0 digit k* per item (first SID token), straight-through soft assignment q, Euclidean quantization zhat_0 = e_{k*}^0 feeding the unchanged deeper RQ stack; side outputs b_i and d_ik for diagnostics.
SAFEGUARDS: Minkowski norm floored at 1e-12 before dividing (b_i = z_i makes identical lifts the common case; must not produce NaN); arccosh argument clamped to [1+1e-7, 1e7]; logits max-shifted before exp; tau = R fixed so logits are dimensionless and no sweep is needed; zero successor rows fall back to b_i = z_i; E initialised at zero and written only for training items; R stored in the checkpoint so Stage 2 and any later encode share the same curvature; negative PMI floors at zero and rows without a positive successor are skipped; the curved selector governs only the stored digit and the straight-through gradient while the reconstruction code is always the Euclidean e_k^0, so assignment and reconstruction can never disagree on the codeword position.
